name: Code Academy Editor Challenge Bank
description: 50 timed editor tasks for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python and React Development. Each successful first completion is worth at least 20 XP and 10 coins.

rewards.policy: Award once per user per challenge using the Code Academy game-platform transaction.

challenges.title: A Proper Welcome Page
challenges.description: Complete the landing-page message so a new learner immediately understands where they are.
requirements: Add an H1 with id="page-title" that says “Welcome to Code Academy”.
Add a paragraph with id="intro" that invites learners to start their coding journey.
Keep the content inside the existing main element.
challenges.hint: Use one clear H1 for the page title and a separate paragraph for the supporting message.

tests.label: The page title is an H1

challenges.title: Build a Course List
challenges.description: Create a concise course list that helps visitors discover the core learning tracks.
requirements: Add four list items inside #course-list.
Include HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Python as list-item text.
Keep the items in a semantic unordered list.
challenges.hint: An unordered list uses ul, and each course belongs in its own li.
challenges.starterCode: Popular courses

challenges.title: Accessible Profile Card
challenges.description: Build a simple profile card with readable text and a properly described profile picture.
requirements: Give the image id="profile-photo" and meaningful alt text.
Set the heading #profile-name to “Ada Lovelace”.
Add a paragraph #profile-role containing “Front-end Developer”.
challenges.hint: The alt text describes the image for people who cannot see it; it should not be empty.

tests.label: The profile photo has useful alt text

challenges.title: Accessible Contact Form
challenges.description: Create a small contact form with labels that are correctly associated with each field.
requirements: Create a form with id="contact-form".
Add required name and email fields with matching label for/id values.
Add a message textarea and a submit button.
challenges.hint: The label for value must exactly match the field id. Use type="email" for an email address.
challenges.starterCode: Contact us

tests.label: Email uses the email input type

challenges.title: Publish a Semantic Article
challenges.description: Use semantic HTML to give a short learning article a clear structure and publication date.
requirements: Wrap the story in an article element.
Add a heading #article-title that includes “Why Practice Matters”.
Add a time element with a valid datetime attribute.
challenges.hint: Semantic elements explain the purpose of content, rather than only how it looks.
challenges.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Article</title></head>
<body><main id="content">
  <!-- Add a semantic article with title, paragraph and publication date -->
</main></body></html>

tests.label: The article has a readable paragraph

challenges.title: Navigation That Goes Somewhere
challenges.description: Build an accessible navigation menu with links to the sections a learner needs most.
requirements: Create a nav element with aria-label="Main navigation".
Add links for Courses, Practice and Progress.
Each link should point to a matching section id on the page.
challenges.hint: The href fragment and the destination section id must match, for example href="#courses" and id="courses".
challenges.starterCode:
Courses

Practice

Progress

challenges.title: A Real Data Table
challenges.description: Present course progress in a table with headers and three data rows.
requirements: Use a table with id="progress-table".
Add header cells for Course and Completion.
Add three body rows, including HTML, CSS and JavaScript; use scope="col" on headers.
challenges.hint: Put header cells in thead and data rows in tbody; use th scope="col" for column headings.
challenges.starterCode: Course progress

challenges.title: FAQ with Native Disclosure
challenges.description: Create two FAQ disclosures that work with the browser without custom JavaScript.
requirements: Add two details elements inside #faq.
Each details element needs a summary question.
Include answers about practice and course progress.
challenges.hint: The details element provides open/close behavior automatically; each one needs a summary.
challenges.starterCode: Frequently asked questions

challenges.title: Compare Three Plans
challenges.description: Build a simple pricing comparison that is understandable to screen-reader users.
requirements: Add three elements with class="plan-card".
Each plan must have a heading, a price and a list of at least two features.
Name the plans Starter, Builder and Pro.
challenges.hint: Keep each plan inside its own article so the page has clear content sections.
challenges.starterCode: Choose your plan

tests.label: Each plan has at least two features

challenges.title: Accessible Image Gallery
challenges.description: Create an image gallery with three figures, captions and meaningful alternative text.
requirements: Add three figure elements inside #gallery.
Every image must have non-empty alt text.
Every figure must include a figcaption.
challenges.hint: A figcaption provides visible context; alt text should describe the image itself.
challenges.starterCode: Learning gallery

challenges.title: Center the Hero Content
challenges.description: Use Flexbox to center a hero message both vertically and horizontally.
requirements: Set .hero to display: flex.
Center items on the cross axis.
Center content on the main axis.
challenges.hint: Flexbox uses align-items for the cross axis and justify-content for the main axis.

challenges.title: Polish the Profile Card
challenges.description: Give a profile card comfortable spacing and rounded corners.
requirements: Set .profile-card padding to 24px.
Set its border radius to 16px.
Give it a visible box shadow.
challenges.hint: Use padding for space inside the card, border-radius for corners and box-shadow for depth.

challenges.title: Lay Out Course Cards with Grid
challenges.description: Make the course collection a clean CSS Grid with even gaps.
requirements: Set .course-grid to display: grid.
Create three equal columns on a wide screen.
Set the grid gap to 16px.
challenges.hint: Try grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)) and gap: 16px.

tests.label: Three equal grid tracks are configured

challenges.title: Design a Clear Primary Button
challenges.description: Create a high-contrast primary button that looks clickable and consistent.
requirements: Use the blue background #2563eb.
Set border-radius to 8px.
Set cursor to pointer and remove the default border.
challenges.hint: Computed styles are checked in the browser, so use a real CSS declaration rather than a comment.

challenges.title: Apply a Dark Theme
challenges.description: Style the page with a dark navy background and soft white text.
requirements: Set the body background to #0f172a.
Set the body text colour to #f8fafc.
Keep the text legible against the background.
challenges.hint: The browser reports computed colours in rgb() form; use the specified hex colours in your CSS.

challenges.title: Align a Navigation Bar
challenges.description: Use Flexbox to align a brand and a navigation group on one row.
requirements: Set .navbar to display: flex.
Use space-between to separate the brand and menu.
Vertically center both sides.
challenges.hint: The two main items are direct children of .navbar, so flexbox can distribute the space between them.

tests.label: Brand and links are spread apart

challenges.title: Make Images Responsive
challenges.description: Prevent an image from overflowing its card on a narrow screen.
requirements: Set max-width to 100%.
Set height to auto to preserve the image ratio.
Ensure the image behaves as a block element.
challenges.hint: max-width limits the rendered width; height:auto keeps the original aspect ratio.

challenges.title: Style a Status Badge
challenges.description: Turn a plain span into a compact pill-shaped status badge.
requirements: Set display to inline-block.
Use 4px 10px padding.
Set the border radius to 999px.
challenges.hint: A very large border-radius creates a capsule shape even when text length changes.

challenges.title: Highlight an Alert
challenges.description: Give an informational alert a distinctive left border and comfortable spacing.
requirements: Set a 4px solid left border.
Set padding to 12px.
Choose a noticeable blue accent colour.
challenges.hint: Use border-left, not the shorthand border, so the challenge checks the intended edge.

challenges.title: Responsive Course Grid
challenges.description: Create a two-column course grid on wide screens and collapse it to one column on narrow screens.
requirements: Use display: grid with a 16px gap.
Make the default grid two columns.
Add a max-width: 600px media query that switches to one column.
challenges.hint: Inside @media (max-width: 600px), override grid-template-columns to 1fr.

tests.label: The mobile rule uses one column
The default grid defines two equal columns

challenges.title: Working Click Counter
challenges.description: Make the counter increase by one each time the learner presses the button.
requirements: Keep the starting count at zero.
On each click, increment the count by one.
Update the #count element without reloading the page.
challenges.hint: Attach a click listener and update textContent; do not replace the whole page.

tests.label: One click changes the count to 1
A second click changes the count to 2

challenges.title: Change a Colour Swatch
challenges.description: Make a button apply the academy teal colour to the swatch when clicked.
requirements: Listen for clicks on #change-color.
Set #swatch background color to rgb(16, 185, 129) (or #10b981).
Keep the existing page structure intact.
challenges.hint: Use element.style.backgroundColor and assign the teal colour after the click.

challenges.title: Add a To-do Item
challenges.description: Turn the task input and button into a small to-do list that ignores blank entries.
requirements: Read and trim the value from #task-input.
Add a new li to #task-list when the input is not blank.
Clear the input after a task is added.
challenges.hint: Use document.createElement("li") and textContent so entered text is treated as text, not HTML.

tests.label: The entered task is added to the list

challenges.fixtureHtml: My tasks

challenges.title: Personalised Greeting
challenges.description: Read a name from a form and show a friendly greeting when the button is pressed.
requirements: Read the value in #name-input.
Show “Hello, {name}!” inside #greeting.
Trim the name so extra spaces are ignored.
challenges.hint: Build the greeting with a template literal and write it to textContent.

tests.label: The learner receives a personalised greeting

challenges.title: Live Character Counter
challenges.description: Update a counter every time a learner types into a message field.
requirements: Listen for input events on #message-input.
Display the current number of characters as “N/40”.
Count the input value, not the placeholder.
challenges.hint: The input event fires for typing, pasting and deleting, so it is more useful than keydown.

tests.label: The live count reflects five characters

challenges.title: Accessible FAQ Toggle
challenges.description: Build a show/hide FAQ answer and keep the button state accessible.
requirements: Toggle the hidden attribute on #faq-panel.
Update aria-expanded from false to true and back.
Keep the button label stable.
challenges.hint: Read button.getAttribute("aria-expanded") to decide the next state, then update both DOM properties.
challenges.fixtureHtml: Practise a little every day.

challenges.title: Reveal a Password
challenges.description: Add a show/hide control that switches the password input between password and text types.
requirements: Clicking #toggle-password changes #password type to text.
Clicking again changes it back to password.
Do not clear the entered value.
challenges.hint: Change the input type property and preserve its current value.

tests.label: Second click hides the password again

challenges.fixtureHtml: <main><label for="password">Password</label><input id="password" type="password" value="abc123"><button id="toggle-password" type="button">Show / hide</button></main>

challenges.title: Add Two Numbers
challenges.description: Read two numeric inputs and display their sum when the Calculate button is pressed.
requirements: Read #number-a and #number-b as numbers.
Show the sum in #sum-result.
Treat empty input as zero instead of NaN.
challenges.hint: Number(input.value) converts a text field to a numeric value.
challenges.fixtureHtml: —

challenges.title: Switch Content Tabs
challenges.description: Make two tabs switch the content panel and expose the selected tab accessibly.
requirements: Clicking #tab-about displays “About our academy”.
Update aria-selected so About is selected.
Use textContent or hidden states to switch the panel.
challenges.hint: Keep the selected state in sync with what is displayed; use aria-selected="true" for the active tab.

tests.label: About tab changes the panel content

challenges.fixtureHtml: Welcome home.

challenges.title: Check a Quiz Answer
challenges.description: Show immediate feedback when a learner checks the correct answer to a simple quiz.
requirements: Listen for a click on #check-answer.
If the checked choice is B, display “Correct answer!” in #feedback.
Keep the feedback region accessible with aria-live.
challenges.hint: Inspect the selected radio input and only show success when its value is B.
challenges.fixtureHtml: Which tag creates a link?

challenges.title: Even or Odd
challenges.description: Complete a function that tells whether an integer is even.
requirements: Define is_even(number).
Return True for even integers and False for odd integers.
Handle zero correctly.
challenges.hint: The remainder operator % gives zero when a number is divisible by two.

challenges.title: Count the Words
challenges.description: Write a function that counts words while ignoring repeated spaces and empty input.
requirements: Define word_count(text).
Split on whitespace rather than one literal space.
Return 0 for a blank string.
challenges.hint: str.split() without an argument handles multiple spaces and newline characters.

tests.label: Five words are counted
tests.code: assert word_count("Code Academy builds coding skills") == 5

challenges.title: Find the Largest Number
challenges.description: Return the largest value in a list of numbers.
requirements: Define find_max(numbers).
Return the largest item without sorting the list.
Handle a list of negative values.
challenges.hint: Track a current maximum and compare each value, or use Python’s built-in max after validating the list.

challenges.title: Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit
challenges.description: Implement the standard temperature conversion formula.
requirements: Define celsius_to_fahrenheit(celsius).
Return celsius × 9/5 + 32.
Return a number, not a formatted string.
challenges.hint: Keep the formula arithmetic numeric; the caller can format the answer later.

challenges.title: Reverse a String
challenges.description: Return the input string in reverse order without modifying the original value.
requirements: Define reverse_text(text).
Support empty text.
Do not print the result; return it.
challenges.hint: Python slicing with a step of -1 can reverse a string.

challenges.title: Count Vowels
challenges.description: Count the vowels in a string regardless of letter case.
requirements: Define count_vowels(text).
Count a, e, i, o and u in either case.
Return zero when no vowels are present.
challenges.hint: Convert to lowercase, then count each character whose value is in "aeiou".

challenges.title: Calculate a Factorial
challenges.description: Calculate the factorial of a non-negative integer.
requirements: Define factorial(number).
Return 1 when number is 0 or 1.
Multiply positive integers up to number.
challenges.hint: Start an accumulator at 1 and multiply it by each integer from 2 through number.

challenges.title: Palindrome Checker
challenges.description: Check whether text reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring spaces and case.
requirements: Define is_palindrome(text).
Ignore spaces and letter case.
Return a Boolean value.
challenges.hint: Normalise with lower() and remove spaces before comparing the text with its reverse.

tests.label: Ordinary phrase is not a palindrome
Long palindrome is detected
tests.code: assert is_palindrome("A man a plan a canal Panama") is True

challenges.title: Apply a Discount
challenges.description: Calculate the final price after a percentage discount.
requirements: Define discounted_price(price, percent).
Subtract the correct percentage from the original price.
Keep decimal prices accurate enough for currency rounding.
challenges.hint: Discount amount is price × percent / 100; subtract that from the original price.

tests.label: 10% off a decimal price is accurate

challenges.title: Summarise Test Scores
challenges.description: Create a summary dictionary for a non-empty list of test scores.
requirements: Define summarize_scores(scores).
Return a dictionary with average, highest and count keys.
Average must be numeric and count must equal the number of scores.
challenges.hint: Compute sum(scores) / len(scores), max(scores) and len(scores).

tests.label: Summary reports the number of scores

challenges.title: Render a Welcome Component
challenges.description: Finish a React component that renders a clear welcome heading and supporting sentence.
requirements: Render an H1 with id="welcome-title" and text “Welcome to Code Academy”.
Add a paragraph that includes “Build skills by coding”.
Keep the component function named App.
challenges.hint: Return JSX from App and use ReactDOM.createRoot to render it into #root.

challenges.title: Render Three Course Cards
challenges.description: Render three course cards from an array instead of repeating the markup manually.
requirements: Create three cards with className="course-card".
Include HTML, CSS and JavaScript in the list.
Use a stable key when mapping the course array.
challenges.hint: Map the courses array and return one article for each course; React uses className, not class.

challenges.title: Stateful Click Counter
challenges.description: Use React state to keep a counter in sync with the displayed number.
requirements: Display the count in #react-count, starting at 0.
Add a button #react-increment that adds one.
Use useState rather than directly editing the DOM.
challenges.hint: Import or use React.useState, then pass a callback to setCount when the button is clicked.

challenges.title: Build a Learner Profile
challenges.description: Create a compact learner profile component with name, level and course track.
requirements: Show a heading #learner-name with “Ama Mensah”.
Show #learner-level containing “Level 3”.
Show #learner-track containing “React Development”.
challenges.hint: Write the content inside the App component and return valid JSX.

challenges.title: React To-do List
challenges.description: Use component state to add a typed task to a list.
requirements: Bind an input to state.
When Add is pressed, append non-empty text to the list.
Clear the field after adding the item.
challenges.hint: Use a tasks array in state and map it to li elements with stable keys.

tests.label: Entered task appears in the list

challenges.title: Toggle Dark Mode
challenges.description: Use state to toggle a class that represents the current theme.
requirements: Start with a main element id="app" and className="light".
Add a button id="theme-toggle".
Clicking the button switches the app class to dark.
challenges.hint: Store the theme in state and change it from light to dark when the button is clicked.

tests.label: Clicking changes the app to dark mode

challenges.title: Controlled Greeting Input
challenges.description: Build a controlled input where the greeting updates as the user types.
requirements: Keep the input value in React state.
The input id must be #react-name.
Show “Hello, {name}” inside #react-greeting as the value changes.
challenges.hint: Set value and onChange on the input; update the state inside onChange.

tests.label: Greeting updates to the typed name

challenges.title: Expandable FAQ Answer
challenges.description: Use state to show and hide an answer in a React FAQ item.
requirements: Keep the answer in an element with id="react-faq-answer".
Clicking #react-faq-button reveals “Practise by building projects”.
Reflect the state using aria-expanded.
challenges.hint: Use a Boolean state value and toggle it when the button is pressed.

tests.label: The answer is no longer hidden

challenges.title: Render a Shopping Basket
challenges.description: Render two shopping items with prices and show the correct total.
requirements: Render two rows inside #basket.
Each row must have className="basket-item".
Display the combined total $45 inside #basket-total.
challenges.hint: The total is 18 + 27. Use array data and map each item to an element.

tests.label: Pen set appears in the basket

challenges.title: Check a React Quiz Answer
challenges.description: Create a small quiz that shows feedback after the learner submits an answer.
requirements: Provide the correct radio choice with id="react-answer-b" and value="B".
On submit, show “Correct answer!” in #react-feedback.
Use React state to track the chosen answer and feedback.
challenges.hint: Use a controlled radio group or onChange handler, then compare the selected value when checking.
